overall: The AG declined to review the January 24 notice as untimely, declined the general specificity allegation, and found no violation in the February 28 notice topics challenged.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the January 24 meeting notice topics were insufficiently specific; it was filed 64 days after that meeting, past the 30-day deadline.
allegations.key_passage: Because the allegation at issue here was filed on March 28, 64 days later, we find that this allegation is untimely and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council's meeting notices generally lacked specificity without identifying which topics were deficient.
allegations.key_passage: Open Meeting Law complaints must allege violations with a degree of specificity, as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the February 28 notice topic 'Council on Aging Director's report' was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic “Council on Aging Director’s report” is simply a time to notify Council members and residents of upcoming events, and that such announcements are generally not pieces of business that Council members anticipate discussing.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the February 28 notice topic 'Other business' was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board’s use of this language on the meeting notice did not violate the law’s requirements.
